*While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

If you have not believed on Jesus Christ as the ONLY means of forgiveness and righteousness, if you have not accepted God's free gift of salvation, if you have been being called to the wedding feast, but have made excuse not to accept, or are trying to work your way in, repent.

Tomorrow is not promised. You are being called today. Don't wait until it is too late. Don't harden your heart.

teachings.title: Today If Ye Will Hear His Voice
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: As unbelief kept Israel out of the promised land, unbelief keeps men from God's rest, which is entered now by faith while the call lasts.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 again builds on the previous; **Hebrews 3**
*For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief*.

*Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.*

Therefore, because, their unbelief in the desert prevented them from entering the promised land, so too fear your unbelief keeping you from entering into the promised land, the rest in Jesus, the better country; the Kingdom of Heaven.

By drawing the comparison to the Hebrews fleeing Egypt with those called coming out of bondage of the law and sin, Paul shows God's grace and His judgment parallels with Exodus spiritually. That it was a picture of Christ that so many Hebrews failed to believe and so died in the wilderness.

For we which have believed do enter into rest. Note the tense. Salvation comes by belief at the moment we call upon His name. At that time we are freed of bondage and given rest, and it is done by the work God finished from the foundation of the world.

**Genesis 2:2**
*And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.*

Paul argues that **if** God says (again quoting **Psalm 95**) *If they shall enter into my rest,* that we can reckon that this is a possible thing, offered by God, **and** those whom it was first preached didn't enter their promised land due to unbelief, **then** we can know we will enter into His rest by faith, and be kept out without it.

And further, as the Spirit moved Paul to write in **Psalm 95**; *Today if ye will hear His voice*, the offer is limited. We have but a short life to believe. A window of His calling, that can pass by death or prolonged neglect to hear His voice. To ignore it. To not retain God in their knowledge. Harden not your hearts when being called.

 *(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

God is reasoning with man, giving us the good news and His terms. Providing examples of what He means, and the if-then logic of it all that none have excuse. Harden not your hearts, hear His voice, NOW is the day of salvation. Believe or be shut out of the promise; never enter into His rest.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: Before it is too late, reprobate
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: The false idea that it is never too late to be saved has led many to Hell, since men who put off grace harden their hearts like Pharaoh, so seek peace in Christ while you can.
teachings.text:
The false idea that it is never too late with God for people to get right and get saved, that as long as you live, there's always a chance for salvation, has led so many to Hell. They put off to tomorrow the gift of grace. They stay in the pleasures of sin for a season, rather than esteeming the reproach of Christ, or having respect for the recompense of the reward.

But rather, like Pharaoh, they harden their hearts and stiffen their necks and dull their hearing. They seek after vain jangling and smooth preaching, and those telling them "peace and safety" when there is no peace.

Like Israel, they chase after idols and put their faith in horses and chariots, turning towards Egypt spiritually. Or worse, pitching their tents towards Sodom.

God's wrath comes like a thief in the night, His judgment is righteous and true. Wake to Him and seek peace in Christ while you can.

Before it is "too late, Reprobate!"

teachings.title: Remember thy Creator before it is too late
teachings.theme: Now is the day of salvation
teachings.summary: Solomon's conclusion that all is vanity calls men to remember their Creator now, before death or the darkened sun of the day of the Lord, when it will be too late to fear Him.
teachings.text:
The end of Solomon's sermon, the preacher has spoken. Life is vanity and vexation of spirit, man toils and dies. There is iniquity and wickedness. Time and chance. A time for every purpose under Heaven. No guarantee of tomorrow. Only fleeting moments of joy where God has blessed us to enjoy the fruits of our labor. We should rejoice in our youth and remember the darkness, reflecting in mourning more than reveling in mirth. We should seek wisdom and reject foolishness, and in all things remember that there is a God, and He is just in His judgment.

And so, Solomon the king and preacher, with his thousands of proverbs, songs and sayings (and wives), sums up the end of the matter. Remember thy Creator. Remember Him in your youth, while it is still light. Before the darkness of this life or the time to come, when it is too late and tribulations and tragedies bring grief and sorrow. Before you die, and it's too late.

Before the day of the Lord.

The sun and the moon and the stars darkening is always a sign of the end, and the 2nd coming of Christ.

**Matthew 24:29-32**
*Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

**Joel 2:31**
*The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come.*

There is a time it is too late to fear the Lord, to get right with Him, to remember our Creator.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

The day of the Lord will see the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men bow, every knee shall bow and tongue confess. The rich men and rulers will beg the rocks and mountains to fall upon them. They shall have their fear come upon them. The music will cease. The streets full of mourning.

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

The grinders shall cease, for there are few...

**Matthew 24:41-42**
*Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left. Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.*

The day of our death or the day of the Lord, the end comes for all men.

*Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern*.

If our bodies are broken, our spine snapped, our skull cracked, our heart stops and we bleed out, if our body can no longer move...And ever the curse of Adam is upon us;

*Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.*

**Genesis 3:19**
*In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

...All things considered, this is the ultimate vanity. *Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.*

The preacher is wise. The wisest man in history, filled with the Spirit of God to know things and the time and treasure to consider all the ways of man under the Sun. He sought understanding and set in order many proverbs, and taught the people knowledge. Seeking truth. Instruction in uprightness. Righteousness.

*The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.*

teachings.title: Absent from the body, present with the Lord
teachings.summary: Believers who die before the resurrection go consciously to Heaven rather than soul sleep, as the damned are in torment now and the souls under the altar cry how long, for created beings remain within time.
teachings.text:
Just to expand upon this point and why I believe the Bible teaches a intermediate stage for those in Christ whose physical body passes away now, before the day of the Lord, before the first resurrection, that our souls go to Heaven, not sleep or instantly regain consciousness at the resurrection as if no time had passed.

Most will agree that the Damned await in hell until the white Throne judgment where by they are cast into the lake of Fire. That their torment is immediate and without cease.

The Bible also talks about The souls of the righteous in Christ crying out "how long?" to God, awaiting His wrath.

Both of these imply that to us, to our souls or to our bodies, flesh or spirit, that we still exist within time as the created. That everlasting and eternal have no meaning outside of time.

That it's only the Creator who exists outside of time, time being a creation itself.

teachings.title: In the resurrection they neither marry
teachings.summary: Jesus answers the Sadducees that resurrected saints are like the angels who cannot marry, angels are never called sons of God, and the saints will judge in the millennial kingdom.
teachings.text:
Continuing Mark chapter 12, we find the Sadducees come to bat, the Pharisees having struck out. They represent the secular Judaism we see today. Reform Jews make up the vast majority of so-called religious Jews, who eschew the spiritual and teach that there is no Heaven or Hell, and no resurrection. They believe they are to become gods on this earth, and teach that by their works, "healing the world" or tikkun olam as they call it, they can make a paradise on Earth where Jews naturally are the leaders of a global kingdom.

It isn't very far removed from the Orthodox Jew/Pharisaical religion of works-based righteousness and their inheritance of an earthly kingdom in the "time to come," just a bit more honest about their worship of self over God.

They seek to trip up Jesus with a very natural man Reddit-tier question regarding the law and the resurrection, thinking the one exposes a flaw in the other, and so bringing the entire thing down.

Jesus shows their sophistry easily. Angels cannot marry, or have relations the way humans do. In the resurrection, our glorified bodies will be like theirs.
(This is an unpopular take in our circles, but I am unmoved in my understanding that the Bible says at no time has God called the angels His sons, they cannot breed, and throughout scripture sons of God always refers to those saved by faith, who called upon His name for salvation, from the time of Seth onward)

Jesus again, being the word made flesh, having perfect understanding of all things as the creator of all things, could not be tested of natural man who cannot receive the things of God as they are spiritually discerned.

We are called to be as knowledgeable in these spiritual matters by understanding of scripture, that when the Kingdom comes, and the millennial reign over Earth takes place, we will serve as judges, stewards over those born in those days. And the least shall be first. The meek shall inherit the kingdom. Those who increased the master's yield by 100 fold will be given much, and those that buried what they were given will rule over nothing. Amen.

So study to show yourself approved unto God that you may be fruitful now, and a good and faithful servant in the Kingdom.

teachings.title: There is hope of a tree
teachings.summary: Job confesses that though man dies, he waits for his change, the resurrection to incorruption, like a cut tree that buds again.
teachings.text:
Job in chapter 14 begins a section of the discourse between he and his erstwhile friends, that continues to show his lament against his bitterness towards life, but starts the process of his proclaiming, in chapter 19, that he knows his Redeemer liveth.

He again notes the brevity of life, that the mortality of men is like a flower cut down or a fleeting shadow. Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean, not one. Not man. Our days are numbered and God is appointed us the bounds that we cannot pass, a day where our flesh will die.

But, job says there is hope of a tree. That even if it's branches rot and the stock die in the ground while the roots still there,  there is hope. A little water can bring it to bud and bring forth boughs again.

Men die and until the heavens be no more they shall not be raised out, until the judgment. Until the end of His wrath is passed.

He says that if he dies, shall he live again? But all the days of his appointed time he will wait till his change comes. This is both the change of death from flesh and the change of being resurrected into eternal life.

After the bounds of his life are come, God will call and he will answer and God will do the desire of the work of His hands, The promise of putting on incorruption.

But he asks, if God is numbered his steps, if God has determined when he will die, then can't He also have watched over his sin? Our sins are as they were sealed up in a bag. Sewn up.

And while a man may die, as God prevail so against us all, though he destroys our Hope and return our bodies to dust, although our sons may come to honor or dishonor, well after our time, in this life, his flesh shall have pain and his soul shall mourn.

What's sadness he has. What wisdom he has in his sadness.

teachings.title: I know that my redeemer liveth
teachings.summary: Job confesses his living Redeemer, Christ, who will stand on the earth, and his hope to see God in his flesh in the resurrection.
teachings.text:
After the merciless railing by Bildad, Job again offers his defense. He lists in all the ways that God has clearly set against him, and the reproach he has become to those around him. His friends, family, kin, wife. All are opposed to him in his sorry state.

Job is destroyed on every side.

He wonders how much more these three friends will continue to break him further with words. He is indignant at their attitudes, that they feel no shame in beating a man when he's down.

He says, if they want to continue to pile on him, know that God has done this and more, and they aren't God. He begs his friends, "Have pity upon me, for the hand of God hath touched me."

This is all he asked for from them. Not belaboring the obvious and accusing him relentlessly, rubbing his nose in his plight.

And then Job makes a general plea to the Heavens, with a profession that is clear:

*Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever! For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth*

We know his words were preserved, forever by the power of God, and his confession of Faith in his living redeemer, his Savior, Who shall stand in the latter day upon the earth. Christ Jesus.

Job says, even after his corrupt flesh is destroyed, his mortal body gone, that in his flesh he shall see God. The resurrection is his hope and he knows he will see it come. His own eyes will witness the Lord in that day. The same blessed hope we share to this day.

And this truth Job holds in his heart, despite all the suffering he has experienced, makes him fear for his erstwhile friends.

If he suffered, be afraid. For the wrath of God is obviously real. And fear it. That rather than their cruelty, they should ask themselves why they do it, given God has done enough. They should fear the same recompense for their behavior, and repent.

teachings.title: Ambassadors of reconciliation
teachings.summary: Our letters of commendation are the souls we win, our glorified body is sure but clothed by our works, and as new men reconciled to God we are ambassadors bringing others the same reconciliation.
teachings.text:
Continuing the theme of the previous chapters, which of you recall, started regarding letters of commendation among men. Paul reminds that our letters of commendation are those who have believed because of our sharing the gospel. He says we are being judged by the conscience of the unbelieving, that our behavior should reflect the light that's within us, living as a light that guides them through the darkness put over them by the devil, winning them to Christ.  That we are ministers of the same Gospel of mercy that changed our hearts and brought us to focus on the things unseen, our conscience clear in Jesus.

Building on this, Paul writes about our physical bodies perishing, but our glorified body from Heaven assured. That the Holy Spirit within us is the earnest, the down payment from God on His promise. But our eternal body is naked, being new born. It is clothed and housed in raiment earned by our works here, judged by God, and so we should constantly strive in this body for that which we will receive in the next.

Preferring being absent this body to be present with the Lord, we should live without fear. What are we threatened with? Heaven? As Jesus said "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." We should live with the confidence that this is true and that we are furnishing the mansion He has provided us, winning souls to Christ.

By focusing on the unseen, living the faith, we also give answer to those that judge by appearance rather than of the heart, as God judges. And in doing so, be able to pierce the veil of darkness and bring them to the light of God reflected in us.

We are a new man, contained in the earthen vessels of the old, but reconciled with God in Jesus, and so, given the ministry, being a servant, to spreading that reconciliation to others. Ambassadors.

Paul says it better than I can, go read the first 5 chapters again.

teachings.title: Hell is real, and Mary had other children
teachings.summary: Jesus preached Hell often, and Matthew 13 names Jesus' brothers and sisters, refuting Mary's perpetual virginity.
teachings.text:
And when Jesus says that the tares should be burned in the fire, the wailing and gnashing of teeth, he is preaching on Hell. Those falsely claiming there is no Hell, or that Christ didn't talk about it are lying. He does frequently, yet many whose heart is by the wayside, or even the stoney ground, blindly believe the lies, having no root in the truth of the word.

As for the Mary worshipers, another L.

*Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?* *And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things?*

His half-brothers and sisters, Mary not a perpetual virgin. Sick and twisted false doctrine rebuked, amen.

teachings.title: Abel's blood sacrifice and Cain's works
teachings.summary: Abel was accepted by faith in the blood sacrifice while Cain was rejected for offering his own works, and the shedding of innocent blood cries out from the earth and brings judgment on a land.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 11:4**
*By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.*

Now fallen, cast out from Eden, Adam and Eve, the mother of man are fruitful and multiply.

And her first born, a man from God is Cain, a tiller of the earth. Working the fields.

We know from Genesis 3 the burden God placed on fallen man.

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

Cain, under this burden grew herbs and vegetables, fruit of the land. With sweat of his brow. *Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the* Lord*.*

And God respected not his sacrifice.

And Abel, a keeper of sheep, *he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the* Lord *had respect unto Abel and to his offering.*

The firstling lamb. The sacrifice of blood for attornment. The Bible says Abel *by faith* brought the sacrifice that was acceptable unto the Lord.

But Cain brought his works and was rejected.

But God, long suffering and who the Bible says would not that any man perish, gives His word to Cain, to repent towards the faith, in the blood of the lamb for remission of sin, as He had given Adam and Eve, that Abel gained God's pleasure by.

*And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.*

Unable to get past his own pride and accept God's promise, His word, Cain allowed his wrath in, and in covetousness slew innocent Abel, and the very earth cries out to the Lord that his blood had been spilled.

This is a Biblical doctrine that's often overlooked. The spilling of innocent blood actually causes the earth itself to cry out to God. We see several times throughout scripture God warns man against it;

*That innocent blood be not shed in thy land, which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.*
**Deuteronomy 19:10**

*For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now*.
**Romans 8:22**

*The blood of their sons and their daughters,*
*Whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan;*
*And the land was polluted with the blood.*
**Psalm 106:38**

One of the things that curses a land and brings judgement on a people is innocent blood shed. It pollutes the land, and the earth travails and groans, crying out to the Lord.

And so undone, Cain is cursed.

When we reject God's word, His gift of salvation in the blood of Christ, the lamb slain at the foundation of the world,  when we count on our works and want credit from God for our own righteousness, we invite sin into our heart, and when we reject God's word finally, are rejected of Him. Marked as Cain.

teachings.title: Blotted Out, Never Added to the Book of Life
teachings.summary: All are born into the book of life and are only blotted out through unbelief, reprobation or unpardonable sin; no one is ever added to it.
teachings.text:
*And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars;*

Again, Jesus is addressing a church, this in Sardis, and He uses descriptors of Himself from scripture to sign the message.

 *I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead.*
*Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.*

The church at Sardis has a reputation for being an active and lively congregation, but Jesus says He knows that's not the case. He warns them to return to what was preached unto them, that they won't die out completely. That His coming won't be a surprise to them, like a thief in the night overtaking them as He will the world of non-believers.

*Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy.*

His appeal then are to the genuinely saved among them in Sardis, encouraging them in their walk, and their reward in His return.

And then, again another message to the saved, who have overcome the world by their faith in Him:

*He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.*

The white raiment of the wedding feast, the garment we receive having been called by grace and accepting the invitation by faith. Whose names are not blotted out of the book of life.

Note, we are born into the book of life, we are blotted out by death as unbelievers, or reprobation, or unpardonable sin such as blasphemy of the Holy Ghost, knowingly adding to or taking away from the word of God or, as we will see, taking the mark of the beast. No one in the Bible is added to the book of life, only blotted out and removed having already been there. Understanding of this helps when faced with a few false doctrines.

Jesus promise to us who are saved is that He will confess our names before our Father, our counsel, the sole mediator we need.

teachings.title: The battle of Armageddon
teachings.summary: At Armageddon Christ defeats the beast's armies with the sword of His mouth, casting the antichrist and false prophet into the lake of fire and leaving the wicked to the fowls.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 13:9**
*Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.*

**Joel 3:12-14**
*Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about. Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.*

*Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.*

Armageddon, the "Mountain of Assembly," refers to Mt Zion. The valley of Jehoshaphat, the valley of judgment, is the space between Zion and Mt Olive, where Christ will rule during the Millennial Reign.

It is here the armies of the beast assemble and ride out to battle Jesus,
King Of Kings, And Lord Of Lords.

*And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.*

The antichrist and his false prophet are instantly cast into the lake of fire. The remnant of their armies slain by the sword that comes from the mouth of Christ. The two-edged sword, which immediately calls to mind the word of God. Spoken from Jesus mouth, with the power to slay the wicked, leaving their carcasses for the carrion birds to feed on.

**Jeremiah 7:33**
*And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.*

**Ezekiel 39:17**
*And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood.*

teachings.title: The Harrowing of Hell is a Catholic fable
teachings.summary: The Catholic Harrowing of Hell misuses 1 Peter 4:6, which in context means the dead in Hell were shown their disobedience by Christ's resurrection, as those mocking Noah were destroyed in the flood.
teachings.text:
There is a false doctrine, invented by Catholics (among dozens of others), called the "Harrowing of Hell." In it, they say that Jesus didn't go to Hell for 3 days and 3 nights to be the burnt sin offering (a holocaust), for the whole world as the sole propitiation for our sins, as the Bible teaches. Instead they claim Jesus went to Hell on a Saturday to give the Gospel to Old Testament saints and various heathens who "lived a righteous life," or were "seekers of truth" like Virgil and Plato and other pagans, so they could go with Him to Heaven.

It is an incredibly natural man thing to believe, and it's no wonder that its origin comes from the false "Gospel of Nicodemus," supposedly written by the unsaved Pharisee in the Gospel of John who couldn't understand salvation and being born again, despite being a leader of the people, as Jesus pointed out.

*Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?*

But to give it some anchor in scripture, they pull **1 Peter 4:6** to claim it. The verse states "*For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead..."* Which relates back to the previous chapter:

**1 Peter 3**
*8 Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:*

*9 Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.*

*10 For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:*

*11 Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.*

*12 For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.*

*13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?*

*14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;*

*15 But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:*

*16 Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

*17 For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.*

*18 For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:*

*19 By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;*

*20 Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.*

*21 The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:*

*22 Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.*

Jesus triumph over death and Hell and the eternal destruction of those in prison, Hell, is a like image to the people destroyed in the flood, the dead in sin, and the quick are those with eternal life in Christ, by the resurrection of Jesus, like Noah and the other 7, saved by water, (which is also a figure of baptism, which is *an answer of a good conscience toward God,* not how we are saved, but that we are saved).

The people in Hell were shown their disobedience by the resurrection of Jesus, just as they mocked Noah and were destroyed by the flood, they mocked God and were thrown into Hell to witness Jesus triumph.

teachings.title: God's patience runs out
teachings.summary: Men and nations who reject God's word and only cry out in calamity find that His longsuffering has an end, and even the backslidden saved can be chastened or taken home.
teachings.text:
In **Jeremiah 37**, we see the king and his princes, those in power besieged by Babylon. They had not harkened to the Lord and did not listen to the wisdom of the word of God, preached by the prophet Jeremiah. But in their calamity they sought him to pray for their salvation from the Chaldean horde.

In a like manner, many men will wait until the foxhole is being shelled to ask God for deliverance. To protect their lives. Even as they reject His word, and salvation of their souls. They shout out "Oh my God!" with no faith. They want to eat their cake and have it too.

But God again and again tells us that He calls early, and often. That wisdom is crying out her voice in the streets.

That, as a mother hen, the Lord seeks to gather us as she would chicks under her wing, but they would not listen. And they slew the prophets and did what they wanted, and so when destruction is due, God laughs at their calamity.

Salvation, be it the individual soul liberty of those justified in Christ, or the physical salvation of a nation, is not extended indefinitely. God is longsuffering. He is mercy and His grace abounds. But He is clear. There comes a time for both people and nations, where His patience runs out and He scourges with a rod of iron. His wrath is kindled. Too late, reprobate.

This has application in the saved Christian's life as well. He wants to form us into vessels fit for His use, that we may bring forth fruit after our kind. But if we resist Him and live for ourselves not heeding His word, separating ourselves to the Gospel, becoming backslidden, being reproached again and again and ignoring it, God will eventually destroy you. Punishment will be more severe for us than the wicked who prosper. Or taking us home earlier than maybe we would have been.

At some point it is too late, even for the saved.

teachings.title: Seek ye the Lord before the day of His anger
teachings.summary: Men are judged after death but nations are judged collectively on earth, so Zephaniah calls all the meek of the earth to seek the Lord before His day of wrath.
teachings.text:
God judges nations. While the judgment of man comes after our physical death (*and it is appointed unto men, once to die, but after this the judgment*).

But the judgment of nations is here on this earth, and is a collective judgment of the people in their land.

The prophets, as we have seen, are sent by God with warnings and rebuke, calling the lost to repentance, nations to reform, Kings to fear the Lord.

Zephaniah is calling the people of Judah, and ultimately all the world, to turn to the Lord in meekness, seeking righteousness.

*Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.*

He warns of the destruction that will befall all nations that have not turned towards Him, and that persecute His people. *The Lord will be terrible unto them.* The burden of the Lord upon the prophet says that men shall worship the Lord, *every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen.*

The prophecy of **Zephaniah 2** is both to the Jews of his time, but also shows that His people are not confined only to them, but of the meek and humble who believe on His name throughout the world.

And the destruction of all nations will be not only to the various nations called out here, but the wrath will be poured out on all the earth against those that transgressed against Him and His people, in the day if the Lord's anger.

The day of the Lord is coming. Christ will return in judgment.

Before the day passes, before the fierce and terrible day of the Lord come, seek ye the Lord. Before it is too late.

teachings.title: The burden of Babylon and the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: Isaiah's prophecy against Babylon has a dual fulfillment, in the fall of the Babylonian empire and in the destruction of the spirit of Babylon in the wrath to come, when no silver or gold can deliver.
teachings.text:
The prophecy of Isaiah against Babylon, they the day of the Lord is at hand, clearly has dual fulfillment. It speaks not only of the destruction of Babylonian empire, which had only risen to prominence in the days of Isaiah, but that same spirit of Babylon which will be destroyed in the wrath to come.

...*cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine. And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.*

**Malachi 3:2**
*But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?*

And as Isaiah preached, the Persians and Medes had no regard for gold and silver, the Lord's judgment can't be swayed either.

**Zephaniah 1:18**
*Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.*

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

teachings.title: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die
teachings.summary: Unlike those who feast in the face of death, believers with the hope of the resurrection embrace separation and discipleship in Christ.
teachings.text:
*And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth: And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.*

The Lord brings His people to a place for repentance, and for mourning their lack of faith and wicked ways that He defend them and repent of the evil He would do unto them. But the people didn't harken, and remained as they were, feasting and drinking in the face of death.

Jesus describes the man who has laid up stores here on earth, prepared as the men of Jerusalem, but it was for naught:

**Luke 12:19-21**
*And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.*

Or as Paul wrote, coming from the other direction; why suffer for God and righteous if there is no hope of the resurrection

**1 Corinthians 15:29-36**
*Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead? And why stand we in jeopardy every hour? I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily. If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die. Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame. But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come? Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die*

That because we are not as others, having no hope we may embrace the separation and discipleship of God in Christ, rather than being as men, most miserable, who say "eat, drink and be merry, for tomorrow we die."

teachings.title: Thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back
teachings.summary: Hezekiah praises God for salvation as a gift of grace, and those who refuse it have no hope, so today is the day to believe on Christ.
teachings.text:
Again, **Isaiah 3**8 retells **2 Kings 20**, and King Hezekiah's illness unto death, his calling upon the Lord to save him, and the grace of God to extend his life 15 years.

With the news from Isaiah, and the sign of the sun moving backwards in its path 10°, Hezekiah praises God.

 *O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these things is the life of my spirit: so wilt thou recover me, and make me to live. Behold, for peace I had great bitterness: but thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back. For the grave cannot praise thee, death can not celebrate thee: they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth.*

Both praise for his healing, but more, the king praises God for His salvation. That men, including himself, had no love of peace. There is none good. All have fallen short of the glory of God.

But in His love, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Salvation was offered, a gift given by grace, and our soul delivered from corruption. Casting all our sins behind us. Reconciled with a perfect and righteous God.

And those who forsake the gift, there is no hope for them. They that go down into the pit, into Hell, cannot hope for the Lord's truth.

Settle with the Lord in the way. Because by judgment, you'll be held to every sin. To the whole debt.

Now is the time. Today is the day. If you don't know for certain that you have eternal life, right now, that can never be lost, repent.

Believe on Christ Jesus. Become one of the living. The children of the Father. Sons of God.

Knowing: *The Lord was ready to save me: therefore we will sing my songs to the stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.*

Rejoice in His salvation. Amen

teachings.title: Isaiah 61, the Christian's mission statement
teachings.summary: The words Jesus read from Isaiah 61 are also every Christian's mission to preach the gospel, before the day of vengeance and the resurrection of the righteous.
teachings.text:
The Lord Jesus read from **Isaiah 61** in the synagogue in Galilee, the scriptures being fulfilled there before them. That the Christ the prophets gave witness to was there before them.

And many asked, "isn't that the carpenter's son?"

I have posted many times before that not only does this proclamation, written in Isaiah, and declared by Jesus, give witness to His ministry and His holy purpose and His wonderful salvation, but also serves as a mission statement for all Christians.

In Him, we are filled with the Spirit. We are anointed Priests of the Lord. We are His Ministers, in Christ.

We are to preach the gospel to the meek, to the poor. To give the good news to the brokenhearted. To preach deliverance to those captive in sin, under the bounds of the law. To bring the lost, who are blind to see, and set them at liberty.

To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.

**John 12:47-48**
*And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.*

Jesus reading Isaiah, leaves off before "*the day of vengeance of our God*."

He was there, in His ministry to bring salvation. But in the last day, when He judges the world by His word, there shall come the day of vengeance.

And in that day, all found to have received His word, who gave been judged and found righteous by His imputed righteousness, will be raised up. Glorified to all nations. Set as rulers over them. Like trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord.

This is a promise of the resurrection. A covenant made with all believers. And for all our troubles and shame for His sake, we will be blessed with a double portion. Everlasting joy shall be upon us.

*I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.*

We, like the seed that dies, and falls, and is sown, we will spring forth, to His glory and praise. Amen.

teachings.title: Though Noah, Daniel and Job were in it
teachings.summary: The righteous stave off a nation's judgment for a time, but when it comes only the saved are spared, though God often spares their families for His purposes.
teachings.text:
Then the Lord gives Ezekiel His word, that when God sets out to destroy a land as wicked as Israel, that even if *Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it,* He would only save them themselves from it.

The illustration that 3 renown righteous men would not be sufficient to save a nation that had backslidden to the point of Judah in this day. No children. No remnant. Only the righteous men themselves.

This establishes a few things that we may know from other scripture. One that, as Abraham argued with the Lord concerning Sodom and Gomorrah, that the presence of the righteous is generally sufficient to stave off judgement, at least for a time. We are the salt of the earth. We preserve the world unto judgment, but eventually it isn't sufficient and God's wrath comes due.

Second, when this judgment comes, only the saved are spared. Only those made righteous by faith in the blood are not appointed to wrath.

Third, it is interesting that Daniel, a contemporary of Ezekiel has, by this time, been noticed of God. It isn't clear that Ezekiel himself may know of Daniel, although the youth was made a president of the Babylonian empire early in captivity. But the Lord knows, and knowing we'd know, he is held up as an example.

Finally, there is a tendency of God's mercy, that when it isn't a final judgment, when it serves His needs, He will save the family of the righteous from that judgment. As 8 were saved by the righteousness of Noah. As Lot's wife (almost!) and his daughters are saved from Sodom. As the remnant of sons and daughters mentioned here in **Exikiel 14**.

*For thus saith the Lord God; How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast? Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be brought forth, both sons and daughters*

The remnant was left for His sake. For His name's sake and the city where He had chosen to place His name. To ensure the line of David continues and that Jerusalem stands, awaiting the Messiah that would come from both, Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: A soft answer and every idle word
teachings.summary: A soft answer and pure words please God, but every idle word will be judged at the Great White Throne, which should drive men to the salvation that spares believers that humiliation.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 15** begins by again establishing the truth that things we say, and the manner we say it, is a key instruction for holy living.

A soft answer, given in kindness and grace can calm a situation. The tongue of the wise uses knowledge and disperses it.

A wholesome tongue, speaking pure words is a tree of life. Both spiritually, by the gospel, but also metaphorically by lifting up others' spirit. Plans and purposes rely on wise counsel, and many counselors make them established.

How we use our mouth, the words we choose, the knowledge we impart, the instruction we give, all is ultimately judged by God.

**Matthew 12:36**
*But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment*.

Because of this, the grievous words that engender strife, stir up anger, or the mouth that pours out foolishness, all is ultimately vanity, and the man who hasn't humbled himself to the Lord, and received justification through Christ will surely be ashamed at the judgment. Imagine every foolish or wicked thing you've ever said in anger, read aloud by the holy God for all to hear.

Every perverse word that causes others' spirit to fall. Every ignorant thing that led others astray. Every contention and strife stirred up by our unwise words, lack of discretion and wisdom, all revealed from the Great White Throne.

I thank God for His great salvation, that spares me from such utter humiliation. This alone should convict man to repentance towards the gospel.

We see that even the thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to God, but pure words are pleasing to Him. A soft answer and pure words, instruction and knowledge, these please the Lord, and they are good to our soul, and are a blessing to the people in our life.

*A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!*

How good it is to hear the joy of a brother when we are feeling down! The comfort in our mourning, being told exactly the thing we needed to hear, with all due wisdom and counsel, this is a gift to all, one we should spread ourselves.

teachings.title: Train up a child in the way he should go
teachings.summary: Training children in the fear of the Lord with the rod of correction, not by osmosis from a weekly service, guards them for life, as prudence means settling one's account with God now.
teachings.text:
The wisdom given Solomon, which he passed on to his son, continues to drive home the lessons of life. The inspired word, *profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*

A good name, being known as upright and honest, is more valuable than the riches life has to offer.

The rich and the poor meet together in death. The Lord is the maker of them all. This perspective is how God sees it, and why He is not a respecter of persons. Why a good name is preferable to gold and silver. Why walking in the way of the Lord is wise, regardless of your station. From the soon to be king, Rheaboham to the least in the kingdom.

A prudent man sees evil coming and hides himself from it, while the simple walk right into it. In the same application of having a good name over riches and knowing the like end of all men, knowing the evil that awaits the wicked, prudence requires making peace with God in the way, before the judgment.

**Matthew 5:25-26** 
*Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison. Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.*

Settle your account with God now, by humility and fear of Him, and you will see riches and honor and life. Better than at the judgment which awaits all, great and small. Rich and poor. Hide yourself from evil, in Christ.

Don't be caught in the thorns and snares in the way of the froward. Their path leads to death. Keep your soul far from their ways.

*Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.* The wisdom of raising Godly children, that they have a healthy fear of the Lord, understanding of what's right, isn't a guarantee of their being righteous in their adulthood, but it certainly is a great inoculation against the snares and stumbling stones most people get caught on.

Christian parents often neglect this, and hope Godliness will be passed on by osmosis from one church service a week. By a few hours a week with a youth group.

Then they panic about what will happen when their child goes off into the world, and face heartbreak when they stray far from the way of God.

Well meaning parents who think they are doing well for their child neglect wisdom, like; *Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.*

Solomon has repeatedly coupled the training up of a child in wisdom and the rod of correction driving foolishness from them, because it is this balance that produces good children.

**Ephesians 6:4**
*And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.*

Note that the Bible does not count spanking a child as "provoking" a child to wrath. Being an unjust and unmerciful ruler of your house does that. Letting them run wild does that.

Because? *He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.*

teachings.title: Boast not thyself of tomorrow
teachings.summary: Tomorrow is not promised, which makes today the day of salvation, so we should not boast or procrastinate nor be paralyzed by worry, but be prudent and diligent now.
teachings.text:
The record of Solomon's wisdom, as recorded by King Hezekiah's scribes, continues in **Proverbs 27**.

The litany of sayings found here offers some new insights, retelling of others and repetition of yet more, all for our edification.

The chapter begins with the understanding that we should not assume what the future brings. We are prisoners of the moment, and our breath is in God's hands. Tomorrow isn't promised.

We primarily use this Biblical understanding to stress the urgency of the gospel when preaching to the lost. That getting your account settled on the way cannot wait. Because, as the Bible says in **2 Corinthians 6:2** ...*I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

If you haven't trusted on Christ as your only means of salvation, given by the grace of the Father, now is the time.

If you have received that precious gift, get to work doing the will of God and winning souls. **Romans 13:11** ..*.now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed*

But even in general terms, boasting about what you will do tomorrow is an empty promise when you don't know what lies in store.

**James 4:14-15**
*Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.*

God willing, it shall come to pass, but better to deal with today, redeem the time and accomplish what may be done now, than seek glory for what you've yet to do. And even then, boast not at all;

*Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.*

It is in the nature of finite man to boast on the morrow while we procrastinate difficult things. To justify our not doing anything now, because of how wonderful our plans are for then. Getting lazy. Saying "If it's God's will" as an excuse.

But what then? Should we not plan for the things that may come? To just wait on the Lord for all things? Not at all. Verse 12;

*A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.*

Some, rather than foolishly passing on, or boasting on what they may do, get so caught up in worry for tomorrow that they are paralyzed today. Jesus teaches us to avoid that as well;

**Matthew 6:34**
*Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.*

We should recognize that the future exists, and the evil thereof, and plan accordingly. Being diligent in the works of today, is being prudent for tomorrow.

*Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.*

This is the correct balance, to see the future as an opportunity that's built in the work of the present, guarding against evil, while knowing the harvest will come. The reward is waiting. The honor and glory will come. Whether serving God and the spiritual works as a laborer for Christ, or just in your daily life in taking care of those things God has put before us.

Achieve balance, seek Him first, be prudent and plan, without worry, don't out off till tomorrow what can be done today. Do not seek your own glory and honor, or boast about what you plan to do, but work diligently knowing you will earn the praise of others, even God, Amen.

teachings.title: Fear God and keep his commandments, the whole duty of man
teachings.summary: After all is vanity, the conclusion is to fear God and keep His commandments, for every work will come into judgment and abundant life is in serving Him.
teachings.text:
All wisdom comes from the Lord. Jesus is that good shepherd. His words are as goads to cattle, the sharp and pronged sticks used to guide the herd. As nails of a master builder, sure and true. Holding the whole house together. Built upon the rock, which Jesus likes His sayings.

The word of God is sufficient to admonish, to guide and be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.

We may write and study an infinite number of books by men, the ways of this world. But the only way we need is God's. Studying to be approved by Him.

*Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.*

Having considered all these things and having observed all he could, knowing there is nothing new under the Sun, and that what is discovered today was known before and will be forgotten and known again in the future, Solomon the Wise comes to the ultimate conclusion that the purpose of life isn't gathering riches, or pleasure or mirth. It is not toil and working endlessly, only to be forgotten. It is only to fear God and keep His commandments. This is the whole duty of man.

**Hebrews 9:27**
*And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment*

**Luke 8:17**
*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

We all have an appointment with death. And a time of judgment before the Lord*, Who will render to every man according to his deeds*.

*For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.*

Vanity, vanity, all is vanity. But faith in the Lord, fearing Him only and keeping His ways and wisdom, in all our ways acknowledging Him that He may direct our paths...this is the secret to life.

As Jesus says in **John 10:10** *...I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.*

With this, the sermon ends. The matter is settled. Life is a gift from God, and an abundant life is in service of Him. The true meaning of it all is to give Him glory. Our purpose is to be known of Him that we may know Christ.

Amen

teachings.title: Search me first, then judge the wicked
teachings.summary: In trouble we should ask God to search us and accept our part, then pray for His judgment on the wicked, for God is angry with the wicked every day.
teachings.text:
Again, David writes a playful song of faith in God to deliver him from evil. And again, the pattern of praise, plea, confession, and confidence in the Lord is present.

Because of their nature, the Psalms are dripping with doctrine. Here we see the faith and confidence in God lends itself to appealing to His mercy and holiness. We learn that we should ask Him to search us. To show us what sins we have in our life, that we may be cleansed and pleasing to Him.

David sings out to the Lord to allow the enemies that compass him about to destroy him, if there is anything he had done to deserve this.

When we are being persecuted or falling into diverse temptations, tests and trials, self-examination should be on our mind. Dealing honestly with ourselves and with God, that maybe it is the result of something we have done. Chastening of the Lord for iniquity in our dealings with others. Sins against the Father. Confession is rewarded by God. He loves an honest soul, humbly seeking Him for forgiveness.

So, like David, call out in crisis, but be willing to accept our role in our calamity, and have a clean conscience towards God. Ask Him to judge you according to your integrity and righteousness, that we don't deceive ourselves. That we don't fall into a victim mentality.

Pray for God's judgment, not only upon you, but your enemies. That His will be done on earth, and upon all people, that He will stand up the righteous and lay low the wicked. Knowing that our defense is of God.

*God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry with the wicked every day.* This important doctrine is a necessary one, to develop a healthy fear of the Lord, the beginning of wisdom.

The same wisdom here that we find so often in David's son, Solomon and his Proverbs.

That those that deal in iniquity will fall victim to their own mischief. The pits they dig for others to fall in will swallow them up. His violence come back upon his own head.

This expectation of God's judgment is a key portion of our faith. Not only the Lord's mercy upon His children, but His wrath on evil-doers.

God is love. But God is also burning vengeance. His anger is kindled and wrath is stored against the wicked.

**Romans 2:2–6**
*But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things. And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God? Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds*

This truth is as important for understanding God as His love. And is why He deserves our praise as we petition Him for our deliverance.

*I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness: and will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high.* Amen

teachings.title: The heavens declare the glory of God
teachings.summary: Creation and conscience reveal God's power and law to all men so that they are without excuse, while His written word gives the hope of mercy and leads to salvation.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 19** is fairly short, yet packed with doctrine, teaching the purpose of creation, the testimony of God to all creatures, the picture of Christ, and the establishment of the law of the Lord in nature itself, that there is no excuse, while the believer is given constant reminders of His judgements.

**Romans 1:18–20**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse*

The heavens declare the glory of God. Looking upon the night sky we see His precision and power. And as the day follows day and night follows night, each with the passing of the sun and the stars, we are given evidence of His might.

The things of creation speak without words, that all man may understand. They don't need a language. They don't need to be explained. Man sees the passage of time, seasons, years, decades even, in heavenly bodies.

The vain hypothetical of a savage on a remote island, never hearing the gospel, is undone by the understanding that all nature is a parable and a testament of God, showing men truth.

The boldness of the sun breaking forth in the morning is as the risen Christ, returning in glory, a picture of the Creator Who is blessed forever, amen.

Nature teaches us God's law. His ways.

**1 Corinthians 11:14**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?*

His wrath is revealed against those who sin, even without the oracles of God documenting His commandments. The Spirit showing mankind the results of their transgressions. The understanding that murder, adultery, lying, stealing, all of these things that do harm to your neighbor and are a shame before God, are known.

**Romans 2:11–16**
*For there is no respect of persons with God. For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law; (For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified. For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.*

Man can see the law of God, know it written in their hearts, watch the outcome of their behavior and the wrath upon those who sin, and know they are guilty before the consuming fire which is God.

How much more are we who have His statutes and commandments by the oracles of God?

**Romans 3:1–2**
*What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.*

The advantage given Israel, and held by the Jews in Paul's day, is now given to the world. That everyone may know His word.

*The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.*

If the day declares His righteousness and the night His knowledge, and the very nature of things speaks to His wrath, then the oracles of God give us the hope of His mercy. God is a rewarder to those that diligently seek Him.

The fear of the Lord is clean, and known to all men. The fool may say in their heart there is no God, but the wise fear Him, even if they don't know scripture.

The truth is more desirable than gold, sweeter than honey. Its pursuit is its own reward, spurring us to seek Him. The warnings and rewards, motivation to learn His ways.

And, in that knowledge, we find His word, and from that word, salvation.

teachings.title: I trusted in thee: let the wicked be ashamed
teachings.summary: In grief and isolation we trust the Lord, who saves us despite our sin, while the wicked who deny Him will be silenced in unquenchable fire.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 31**, picking up in verse 9. The gladness and rejoicing in God's mercy and crying out to Him in the earlier stanzas, brings us the heart of the matter, the trouble in David's life, and reflected in our own struggles.

He says I am in trouble, consumed with grief and physically and spiritually affected by the tribulation in his life. This is something everyone alive can relate to. Anyone alive long enough to be broken hearted. Betrayed. Lied about and persecuted.

*For my life is spent with grief, and my years with sighing: my strength faileth because of mine iniquity, and my bones are consumed.*

When we are going through it, it can feel as though all we ever have known is grief. We can feel all alone, when not only our enemies abandon us, but our neighbors and friends won't even look at us. So miserable and alone.

We may feel forgotten as a dead man, out of sight out of mind. Truly miserable. Feeling as though the whole world has conspired against us. Having no where to turn or anyone to trust.

*But I trusted in thee, O LORD: I said, Thou art my God.* What a beautiful reminder that we have a friend in Jesus. We have a Lord who is trustworthy and Who cares. Whose face shines on us, and saves us. Not because of how good we are, but despite our sin. For His mercies' sake. Because He so loved us.

We plead, *Let me not be ashamed, O LORD; for I have called upon thee*, and we know that God, Who cannot lie, has promised us deliverance. L*et the wicked be ashamed, and let them be silent in the grave.* We will sing His praise forever, while they are tormented by unquenchable fire, where the worm dieth not.

**Isaiah 66:24**
*And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.*

**Mark 9:47–49**
*And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.*

All those that have denied the truth of God shall be silenced. They shall be made to be ashamed. Let the wicked be ashamed, but we have trusted the Lord.

*Let the lying lips be put to silence; which speak grievous things proudly and contemptuously against the righteous.*
